knowledge:
- key_parameters: type=the data type of the out-of-memory structure (e.g., "double", "int32") ;; path=the file path(s) where the binary data is stored ;; offset=the byte offset(s) within the file(s) ;; extent=the number of data elements at each file/offset ;; rowMaj=logical indicating if matrix is row-major (default is column-major) ;; index=observed domain values (e.g., m/z values) for nonuniform signals ;; domain=effective/shared domain values for resampling/reindexing ;; sampler=resampling method (e.g., "max") for sparse matrices ;; tolerance=tolerance for matching/binning/merging peaks or alignment ;; snr=signal-to-noise ratio threshold for peak detection ;; noise=noise estimation method (e.g., "diff", "filt", "sd", "mad") in findpeaks
- alternatives: Cardinal=a domain-specific Bioconductor package built on top of matter for statistical analysis of mass spectrometry imaging experiments
- when_to_use: Use when datasets (dense/sparse matrices, arrays, lists) are larger than the available RAM (larger-than-memory/out-of-core computing), or when processing nonuniformly-sampled signals (e.g., mass spectra with varying m/z axes, LC-IMS-MS data) or performing 1D/2D signal/image processing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak detection, alignment).
- pitfalls: Iterating over a matrix in the direction opposite to its data orientation (e.g., row-wise on a column-major matrix) is much slower; use rowMaj() to check orientation. ;; Character vector elements in matter_list are limited to scalar strings due to out-of-memory complexities. ;; Signal warping (warp1_loc) is highly sensitive to the tol (tolerance) parameter. ;; In noisy signals, simple local maxima detection (locmax) will yield many more false peaks than true peaks; noise estimation and SNR filtering are required. ;; filtn_* functions (using KNN search for N-dimensional nonuniform signals) are computationally intensive.

workflows.name: out_of_memory_tensor_operations
workflows.intent: Create out-of-memory dense and sparse matrices/arrays and perform deferred arithmetic.
input: raw_data.bin (binary file containing large matrix or array data)
workflows.stages: 1. Create out-of-memory array using matter_arr or matrix using matter_mat ;; 2. Transpose or check major order using t and rowMaj ;; 3. Perform deferred arithmetic operations ;; 4. Create sparse matrices using sparse_mat with or without pointers
workflows.code:
x <- matter_vec(1:10)
y <- matter_vec(11:20)
z <- cbind(x, y)
atomdata(z)

set.seed(1)
a1 <- array(sort(runif(24)), dim=c(4,3,2))

a2 <- matter_arr(a1)
a2

path(a2)

a3 <- matter_arr(type="double", path=path(a2), offset=0, extent=10)
a3

a1[1:10]

set.seed(1)
m1 <- matrix(sort(runif(35)), nrow=5, ncol=7)

m2 <- matter_mat(m1)
m2

m3 <- matter_mat(type="double", path=path(m2), nrow=7, ncol=5, rowMaj=TRUE)
m3

t(m2)

rowMaj(t(m2))
rowMaj(m2)

m2 + 100

as.matrix(1:5) + m2

t(1:7) + m2

set.seed(1)
s1 <- matrix(rbinom(35, 10, 0.05), nrow=5, ncol=7)

s2 <- sparse_mat(s1)
s2

atomdata(s2)
atomindex(s2)

s3 <- sparse_mat(atomdata(s2), index=atomindex(s2), nrow=5, ncol=7)
s3

s4 <- sparse_mat(s1, pointers=TRUE)
atomdata(s4)
atomindex(s4)
pointers(s4)

s5 <- sparse_mat(atomdata(s2), index=atomindex(s2), pointers=pointers(s2), nrow=5, ncol=7)
s5

workflows.name: nonuniform_spectral_signal_processing
workflows.intent: Represent nonuniformly-sampled spectral signals on a common domain, perform smoothing, baseline removal, alignment, peak detection, and binning/merging.
input: spectra_list.rds (list of nonuniformly-sampled spectral signals with varying m/z values)
workflows.stages: 1. Align nonuniform signals to a common domain using sparse_mat or sparse_vec ;; 2. Smooth 1D signals using filt1_* functions ;; 3. Estimate and subtract baseline using estbase_* functions ;; 4. Align/warp signals to a reference using warp1_loc ;; 5. Detect peaks using findpeaks with noise estimation ;; 6. Bin and merge peaks across multiple spectra using binpeaks and mergepeaks
workflows.code:
set.seed(1)
s <- replicate(4, simspec(1), simplify=FALSE)

head(domain(s[[1]]))
head(domain(s[[2]]))
head(domain(s[[3]]))
head(domain(s[[4]]))

mzr <- range(
    domain(s[[1]]),
    domain(s[[2]]),
    domain(s[[3]]),
    domain(s[[4]]))
mz <- seq(from=round(mzr[1]), to=round(mzr[2]), by=0.2)

index <- list(
    domain(s[[1]]),
    domain(s[[2]]),
    domain(s[[3]]),
    domain(s[[4]]))

spectra <- sparse_mat(s, index=index, domain=mz,
    sampler="max", tolerance=0.5)

spectra

spectra / t(colMeans(spectra))

set.seed(1)
s <- simspec(1, sdnoise=0.25, resolution=500)

filt1_ma(s)
filt1_gauss(s)
filt1_bi(s)
filt1_diff(s)
filt1_guide(s)
filt1_pag(s)
filt1_sg(s)

set.seed(1)
s <- simspec(1, baseline=5, resolution=500)

estbase_loc(s)
estbase_hull(s)
estbase_snip(s)

set.seed(1)
s <- simspec(8, sdx=5e-4)

ref <- rowMeans(s)
s2 <- apply(s, 2L, warp1_loc,
    y=ref, events="max", tol=2e-3, tol.ref="y")

set.seed(1)
s <- simspec(1)

i1 <- findpeaks(s, snr=3, noise="diff")
i2 <- findpeaks(s, snr=3, noise="filt")
i3 <- findpeaks(s, snr=3, noise="sd")
i4 <- findpeaks(s, snr=3, noise="mad")

set.seed(1)
s <- simspec(4)

peaklist <- apply(s, 2, findpeaks, snr=3)

peaks <- binpeaks(peaklist)
as.vector(peaks)

peaks <- mergepeaks(peaks, tol=1)
as.vector(peaks)

workflows.name: image_processing_and_alignment
workflows.intent: Smooth, enhance contrast, and warp/co-register 2D images.
input: image_matrix.rds (2D matrix representing spatial imaging data)
workflows.stages: 1. Smooth 2D images using filt2_* functions ;; 2. Enhance image contrast using enhance_* functions ;; 3. Warp and co-register images using warp2_trans ;; 4. Detect 2D local maxima using knnmax
workflows.code:
set.seed(1)
img <- volcano + rnorm(length(volcano), sd=2.5)

filt2_ma(img)
filt2_gauss(img)
filt2_bi(img)
filt2_diff(img)
filt2_guide(img)

set.seed(1)
img <- volcano + rlnorm(length(volcano), sd=1.5)

enhance_adj(img)
enhance_hist(img)
enhance_adapt(img)

img1 <- trans2d(volcano, rotate=15, translate=c(-5, 5))

img2 <- warp2_trans(img1, volcano)

set.seed(1)
dm <- c(64, 64)
img <- array(rnorm(prod(dm)), dim=dm)

coord <- expand.grid(lapply(dim(img), seq_len))

i <- knnmax(img, index=coord, k=49)
i <- which(i, arr.ind=TRUE)
